claims.text: DFT simulations can facilitate production of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
DFT can identify stable NM-HEA configurations.
The initial NM-HEAs are in a disordered, non-equilibrium state.
GGA-PBE is an applicable exchange-correlation functional for the proposed NM-HEA simulations.
A plane-wave cutoff energy of approximately 500 eV is suitable for the proposed simulations.
A 5x5x5 Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid is suitable for the proposed simulations.
Predicted stable NM-HEA configurations can guide experimental synthesis.
DFT predicts the thermodynamic stability of different NM-HEA configurations.
Identifying the most stable structures through DFT can guide synthesis of three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
DFT-guided synthesis will increase the yield of NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control by 30% relative to previous synthesis methods.
HRTEM and XPS can be used to assess the claimed yield and precise atomic control.
The proposed approach applies to NM-HEAs containing up to five different noble metals.
The proposed approach applies to nanoframeworks with pore sizes from 5 to 20 nm.
DFT prediction accuracy may depend on the exchange-correlation functional and other simulation parameters.
Experimental synthesis may not perfectly reproduce the DFT-predicted structures.
The hypothesis is designated as falsified if the yield improvement is less than 20% relative to previous synthesis methods.
